back: Refers to people; can be subject, object, or complement [10].
Formal alternative to 'who' as object or after prepositions [10].
Use 'which' to identify somebody in a group [10].
Prefer 'which' when there is a choice between two or more specific things/people [10].
Verb is usually singular after 'who' or 'what' as subject, even if plural answer expected [10].
'How was the journey?' (opinion) vs 'What was the journey like?' (opinion) [10].
Used before a verb or noun to ask about ownership/responsibility [10].
In formal contexts: 'In whose house was it found?' [10].

front: To ... should the documents be sent?
Which / Who ... of you is Dr Hansen?
